In developing Tweedie functions for queuing models (see `ramp.falciparum`), we use zero truncated functions to model the multiplicity of exposure (MoE). 


```{r}
library(ramp.func)
```

## Zero Truncated Poisson

```{r}
x <- 1:20
dx <- dPOIStrunc(1:20, 1)
sum(dx)
```

```{r}
sum(x*dx)
```


```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
F_moe <- make_POIStrunc(1)
plot(F_moe(1:20), type = "h", lwd=2, 
     ylim = c(0, F_moe(1)), xlab = "x", 
     ylab = expression(F[MoE]))
```

## Zero Truncated Negative Binomial 

```{r}
x <- 1:40
dx <- dNBtrunc(x, 1, .5)
sum(dx)
```

```{r}
sum(x*dx)
```

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
F_moe <- make_NBtrunc(1, .5)
plot(F_moe(1:20), type = "h", lwd=2, 
     ylim = c(0, F_moe(1)), xlab = "x", 
     ylab = expression(F[MoE]))
```
